latest.title: Oobit Lets AI Assistants Pay with Stablecoins Via One-Time Cards - The Fintech Times
latest.summary: * Oobit Lets AI Assistants Pay with Stablecoins Via One-Time Cards. #### ***Oobit**, a Singapore-based stablecoin payments firm, has launched Oobit AI Payments, a product that lets users authorise AI ...
highlights: * Oobit Lets AI Assistants Pay with Stablecoins Via One-Time Cards. #### ***Oobit**, a Singapore-based stablecoin payments firm, has launched Oobit AI Payments, a product that lets users authorise AI assistants to make purchases on their behalf using stablecoins, without granting those assistants access to the underlying account balance or primary payment credentials.*. When a user asks an AI assistant to book, buy or pay for something, the assistant flags the transaction for approval. Once the user confirms, Oobit generates a one-time virtual card tied exclusively to that transaction. The AI receives the card details it needs to complete checkout; it never holds the user’s wallet credentials or sees the broader account. The one-time card model is not new in isolation. What Oobit is doing is applying that architecture to the consumer-facing AI agent context and running it on top of stablecoin settlement rather than traditional card rails.

week.title: Musing Ourselves to Death - The Atlantic
week.summary: AI agents are doing our shopping for us, and wreaking havoc on the internet. You wake up to a notification that a grocery-store employee will deliver all of the ingredients for the three recipes you s...
highlights: AI agents are doing our shopping for us, and wreaking havoc on the internet. You wake up to a notification that a grocery-store employee will deliver all of the ingredients for the three recipes you saved last night to your “Weeknight Dinner” folder. While you brew your coffee, a program browses online retailers to compare toilet-paper prices, and another solicits competitive bids for Sheetrock work you need done in the garage. On your lunch break, you get an alert that computers acting on your behalf noticed some unclaimed funds and class-action payouts in a state database and claimed them. By the time you get home, the groceries are on your doorstep, and you’ve gotten back $150. This is the future that OpenAI, Meta, xAI, Google, and the rest are selling with a spate of always-on AI assistants that work for you. A few weeks after Muse’s launch, OpenAI launched its competing product, Dots, which Sam Altman claimed would let you “get more of your time and attention back.”.

highlights: 5. Google’s Gemini 4 Argon back at frontier: Google scrambled back to the frontier with its latest Google Gemini 4 Argon model. It is Google’s first major frontier release since Gemini 3 late last year, and Google says it beats OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic’s Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 on coding, science, finance and law. Independent tests are less generous: the Artificial Analysis Index has Argon at 53, tied with Astra, behind Opus 5.5 and Meta’s Muse Wonder Full, as I laid out in AI-RTZ [...] laid out in AI-RTZ #1238. Google is pricing to win, at about a fifth of Astra and Fable for now, and it landed a day after Meta’s Wonder. Two frontier launches in two days. My take, from ARD #183: expect frontier leadership to keep ebbing and flowing, in an infinite game, not a race. Google is unique, with a full vertical stack from chips to billions of users, so it can afford to arrive late, and cheap. Its core goal is still ‘good enough’ models for the billions, as I said in ARD #175, while [...] 3. month.title: Musing Ourselves to Death - The Atlantic
month.summary: AI agents are doing our shopping for us, and wreaking havoc on the internet. You wake up to a notification that a grocery-store employee will deliver all of the ingredients for the three recipes you s...
highlights: AI agents are doing our shopping for us, and wreaking havoc on the internet. You wake up to a notification that a grocery-store employee will deliver all of the ingredients for the three recipes you saved last night to your “Weeknight Dinner” folder. While you brew your coffee, a program browses online retailers to compare toilet-paper prices, and another solicits competitive bids for Sheetrock work you need done in the garage. On your lunch break, you get an alert that computers acting on your behalf noticed some unclaimed funds and class-action payouts in a state database and claimed them. By the time you get home, the groceries are on your doorstep, and you’ve gotten back $150. This is the future that OpenAI, Meta, xAI, Google, and the rest are selling with a spate of always-on AI assistants that work for you. A few weeks after Muse’s launch, OpenAI launched its competing product, Dots, which Sam Altman claimed would let you “get more of your time and attention back.”.
